item.name: Lantern of Last Echoes
item.description:
An ornate brass-framed lantern holds cloudy teal glass and a pale, smokeless flame. A skull-shaped face decorates its cage. Old investigators of the river trade used such lanterns to reconstruct disasters and disappearances.

While the shutter is open, the lantern’s flame sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for the next 20 feet. The flame stays with the lantern, requires no fuel or oxygen, and gives off no heat. An Interact action opens or closes the shutter, revealing or concealing that flame.

Passive: While the shutter is open, you gain the [Oddity Identification](link_feat_20375) skill feat. It works as that feat normally does.

Activate—[Light](link_spell_4699) (two actions, concentrate, manipulate). Effect: you cast light, creating a separate orb. The orb uses the spell’s radius, range, and duration, and you can sustain the spell to move it or attach it to a willing creature. The lantern’s own flame is unaffected.

Activate—Final Glimmer (two actions, concentrate, manipulate). Frequency three times per day. Requirements: you are within 10 feet of identifiable physical remains of a creature that died within the past 7 days. Effect: the lantern projects a silent image of one sensory fragment from the creature’s final moments, chosen by the GM. The image lasts up to 6 seconds and provides at least one concrete, truthful clue. Eligible remains always yield a clue; no check is required.

The image cannot communicate, answer questions, disclose thoughts, or reproduce legible writing. It can show an attacker’s outline or visible features but does not supply a name or confirm an identity. The lantern draws a lingering echo from the remains; it neither summons nor speaks to the dead.

Special: no investment or spellcasting is required. These activations have no effect on thralls and do not modify necromancer class abilities. Final Glimmer’s uses belong to the item and do not refresh when passed to another creature.

ancestry.name: Dwarf
ancestry.description:
> _Dwarves are a short, stocky people who are often stubborn, fierce, and devoted._

Dwarves have a well-earned reputation as a stoic and stern people, but they also have an unbridled zeal and deeply value artisanship. To a stranger, they can seem untrusting and clannish, but to their friends and family, they are warm and caring. While trust from a dwarf is hard-won, once gained it is as strong as iron.

If you want to play a character who is as hard as nails, a stubborn and unrelenting adventurer, with a mix of rugged toughness and deep wisdom, you should play a dwarf.

background.name: Acolyte
background.description:
> _You spent your early days in a religious monastery or cloister. You may have traveled out into the world to spread the message of your religion or because you cast away the teachings of your faith, but deep down, you'll always carry within you the lessons you learned._

Choose two attribute boosts. One must be to **Intelligence** or **Wisdom**, and one is a free attribute boost.

You're trained in the Religion skill and the Scribing Lore skill. You gain the [Student of the Canon](link_feat_20599) skill feat.

class.name: Fighter
class.description:
> _Fighting for honor, greed, loyalty, or simply the thrill of battle, you are an undisputed master of weaponry and combat techniques. You combine your actions through clever combinations of opening moves, finishing strikes, and counterattacks whenever your foes are unwise enough to drop their guard. Whether you are a knight, mercenary, sharpshooter, or blade master, you have honed your martial skills into an art form and perform devastating critical attacks on your enemies._

* * *

### **During Combat Encounters…**

You strike with unmatched accuracy and use specialized combat techniques. A melee fighter stands between allies and enemies, attacking foes who try to get past. A ranged fighter delivers precise shots from a distance.

### **During Social Encounters…**

You can be an intimidating presence. This can be useful when negotiating with enemies, but is sometimes a liability in more genteel interactions.

### **While Exploring…**

You keep up your defenses in preparation for combat, and keep an eye out for hidden threats. You also overcome physical challenges in your way, breaking down doors, lifting obstacles, climbing adeptly, and leaping across pits.

### **In Downtime…**

You might perform manual labor or craft and repair armaments. If you know techniques you no longer favor, you might train yourself in new ones. If you've established your reputation, you might build an organization or a stronghold of your own.

### **You Might…**

*   Know the purpose and quality of every weapon and piece of armor you own.
    
*   Recognize that the danger of an adventurer's life must be balanced out with great revelry or ambitious works.
    
*   Have little patience for puzzles or problems that require detailed logic or study.
    

### **Others Probably…**

*   Find you intimidating until they get to know you—and maybe even after they get to know you.
    
*   Expect you're all brawn and no brains.
    
*   Respect your expertise in the art of warfare and value your opinion on the quality of armaments.

content._README: Here's some compiled data about the character. Should be fairly human-readable. The <character> section is what WG reads, this section is solely for you! Should give you an abundance of compiled stats and info about the character. If you have any questions, feel free to ask on our Discord!

all_sources.name: Player Core
all_sources.description: The Pathfinder Player Core presents a new entry point to Pathfinder Second Edition, with everything a player needs to learn how to play the game! Choose from eight ancestries, eight complete character classes, and hundreds of feats and spells to make unique characters ready for deadly adventures in a world beset by magic and evil! This 464-page hardcover tome is the definitive rules resource for all Pathfinder Second Edition players!

all_sources.name: Common Core
all_sources.description: Content that's shared between Pathfinder Second Edition and Starfinder Second Edition.

all_sources.name: GM Core
all_sources.description: Unleash your imagination, creating worlds and stories beyond measure with the new Pathfinder GM Core for Pathfinder Second Edition! This comprehensive 336-page hardcover rulebook gives Game Masters everything they need to craft thrilling tales of adventure, from a single-night’s dungeon delve to complex epics spanning years. Within these pages you’ll find clear guidelines for creating new hazards and monsters, tools to design challenging, balanced encounters, and rules for rewarding characters for the dastardly challenges you array before them! Pathfinder GM Core also contains a dragon’s hoard of magic items and treasure to entice and reward your players, from simple healing potions to magic weapons and armor and legendary artifacts, including dozens of brand-new items!

all_sources.name: Monster Core
all_sources.description: Heroes are defined by their foes—from shambling skeletons to terrifying dragons, each enemy leaves a mark on their growing legend. Make your legends memorable with foes from the new Pathfinder Monster Core rulebook for Pathfinder Second Edition! This 376-page hardcover book is packed with a wide range of monsters useful to all Pathfinder campaigns, giving the Game Master plenty of threats to throw at their adventurers, at any level of experience. The lavishly illustrated tome also includes guidelines for reading monster entries and adjusting existing monsters to tailor fit your story! This is the definitive resource for Pathfinder Second Edition monsters!

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Oddity Identification
generalAndSkillFeats.description: When you become aware of a magical effect or see a spell being cast, you can immediately determine if it twists minds (with the [mental](link_trait_1448) trait), fights against fortune (with the [fortune](link_trait_1460) or [misfortune](link_trait_1677) trait), or reveals secrets (with the [detection](link_trait_1508), [prediction](link_trait_1896), [revelation](link_trait_1907), or [scrying](link_trait_1590) traits). At the GM's discretion, similar effects can also fall into these categories. When you [Identify Magic](link_action_19730) or [Recall Knowledge](link_action_19753) to learn more about these effects, you can always use [Occultism](link_trait_1514) without penalty and gain a +2 circumstance bonus.

rules.label: Oddity Identification (identify magic with specific traits)

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Shield Block
generalAndSkillFeats.trigger: While you have your shield raised, you would take physical damage (bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing) from an attack.
generalAndSkillFeats.description: You snap your shield in place to ward off a blow. Your shield prevents you from taking an amount of damage up to the shield's Hardness. You and the shield each take any remaining damage, possibly breaking or destroying the shield.

generalAndSkillFeats.name: Student of the Canon
generalAndSkillFeats.description: You've researched many faiths enough to recognize notions about them that are unlikely to be true. If you roll a critical failure at a Religion check to [Decipher Writing](link_action_19622) of a religious nature or to Recall Knowledge about the tenets of faiths, you get a failure instead. When attempting to [Recall Knowledge](link_action_19753) about the tenets of your own faith, if you roll a failure, you get a success instead, and if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead.

classFeats.name: Reactive Strike
classFeats.trigger: A creature within your reach uses a manipulate action or a move action, makes a ranged attack, or leaves a square during a move action it’s using.
classFeats.description: You lash out at a foe that leaves an opening. Make a melee [Strike](link_action_19856) against the triggering creature. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a [manipulate](link_trait_1433) action, you disrupt that action. This [Strike](link_action_19856) doesn’t count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn’t apply to this [Strike](link_action_19856).

classFeatures.name: Reactive Strike
classFeatures.description: Ever watchful for weaknesses, you can quickly attack foes that leave an opening in their defenses. You gain the [Reactive Strike](link_feat_19751) reaction.

classFeatures.name: Shield Block
classFeatures.description: You gain the [Shield Block](link_feat_20534) general feat, a reaction that lets you reduce damage with your shield.

physicalFeatures.name: Clan Dagger
physicalFeatures.description: You get one [clan dagger](link_item_6796) for free, as it was given to you at birth. Selling this clan dagger is a terrible taboo and earns you the disdain of other dwarves.

character_traits.name: Humanoid
character_traits.description: Humanoid creatures reason and act much like [humans](link_trait_1436). They typically stand upright and have two arms and two legs.

character_traits.name: Dwarf
character_traits.description: This indicates content from the dwarf ancestry.

character_traits.name: Occult
character_traits.description: This magic comes from the occult tradition, calling upon bizarre and ephemeral mysteries. Anything with this trait is [magical](link_trait_1504).

sense.name: Darkvision
sense.description: A creature with darkvision can see perfectly well in areas of darkness and dim light, though such vision is in black and white only. Some forms of magical darkness, such as a 4th-rank [darkness](link_spell_4552) spell, block normal darkvision.

sense.name: Darkvision
sense.description: A creature with darkvision can see perfectly well in areas of darkness and dim light, though such vision is in black and white only. Some forms of magical darkness, such as a 4th-rank [darkness](link_spell_4552) spell, block normal darkvision.

sense.name: Hearing
sense.description: Hearing is the ability to perceive sound by detecting vibrations through an organ such as the ear. A creature might be undetected by you if it’s in an environment that distorts the sense, such as a noisy room. In those cases, you have to use the [Seek](link_action_19845) basic action to detect the creature.

data.text: whenever you’re trying to locate an undetected creature that is within the range of your scent

sense.name: Scent (imprecise 30 ft)
sense.description:
You can use your sense of smell to determine the location of a creature. The GM will usually double the range if you’re downwind from the creature or halve the range if you’re upwind.

In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks whenever you’re trying to locate an undetected creature that is within the range of your scent.

spell.name: Light
spell.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can [Sustain](link_action_19858) the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can [Dismiss](link_action_19627) the spell. If you [Cast the Spell](link_action_19611) while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

text.text: The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).
